edges.limitations: Mice carry two functional MBL genes (Mbl-A and Mbl-C) where humans express one product, so profound deficiency requires combined knockout rather than a single-gene lesion; the intravenous lethal inoculum is far more severe than typical human exposure; and the model reproduces a profound, fully penetrant deficiency rather than the common, low-penetrance human state this entry describes.

nodes.description: The defining laboratory abnormality: low circulating MBL antigen and low mannan-dependent lectin-pathway activity, congenital and lifelong though it can rise as an acute-phase reactant. There is no universal threshold - reported "deficiency" cutoffs span <50 to <600 ng/mL and one study set it at <0.6 mg/L - so the proportion called deficient depends heavily on the assay and cutoff.

nodes.description: MBL is functional only as higher-order oligomers (tetramers to hexamers of structural units) that present multiple carbohydrate-recognition domains for high-avidity binding. The exon-1 variants disrupt the collagen-like helix so that only low-order, largely noncovalent assemblies form, and these bind microbial carbohydrate ligands with markedly reduced capacity. This was shown directly in recombinant protein expressed in Chinese hamster ovary cells.

nodes.description: Surface-bound MBL carries MASP-1 and MASP-2; on clustering, MASP-1 autoactivates and is the physiological activator of MASP-2, and MASP-2 then cleaves C4 and C2 to build the C4b2b (C4b2a) C3 convertase that deposits C3b. Reduced functional MBL means less of this lectin-pathway C3-convertase activity and so less C3b deposition, while the classical and alternative pathways and total complement (CH50/AH50) are typically preserved. In human pneumococcal meningitis, cerebrospinal-fluid MBL level correlated with C3a and iC3b, direct evidence that lectin-pathway MBL drives complement activation in people and not only in vitro.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic variation and cerebrospinal fluid levels of mannose binding lectin in pneumococcal meningitis patients.
evidence.snippet: CSF MBL levels were positively correlated with C3a and iC3b levels, indicating complement activation by the lectin pathway.

nodes.description: This is the gating node that makes MBL deficiency a susceptibility state rather than a disease. Reduced lectin-pathway opsonisation produces recurrent or unusually severe infection chiefly when a second factor removes compensating redundancy: early infancy (roughly 6-18 months, after maternal antibody wanes but before adaptive immunity matures), chemotherapy-induced neutropenia, transplantation and other immunosuppression, or a coexisting antibody or structural lung defect. In isolation the deficiency is usually silent, which is why the downstream phenotype edges are drawn from this node and not directly from the molecular lesion.

nodes.description: The three exon-1 missense alleles - D (rs5030737, p.Arg52Cys), B (rs1800450, p.Gly54Asp) and C (rs1800451, p.Gly57Glu), collectively called O - fall in or adjacent to the collagen-like region and change MBL structure and serum concentration; the -221 X promoter allele (rs7096206) lowers transcription. These are common population variants rather than rare highly penetrant loss-of-function mutations, and ClinVar carries discordant assertions for them, which is why the functional impact is recorded as a partial loss of function.

nodes.description: Mice devoid of all MBL activity were generated to test MBL's role in host defence directly in vivo. On intravenous Staphylococcus aureus challenge, MBL-null mice showed greatly increased mortality, and neutrophils together with MBL were required to limit infection.

Invasive pneumococcal disease including meningitis is enriched in people homozygous for defective MBL2 genotypes. The signal is pathogen-specific: the same deficiency does not increase invasive meningococcal disease, which the entry records as a REFUTE item to keep the pathogen-dependence visible. nodes.description: Recurrent upper- and lower-respiratory infection is the most frequently reported clinical correlate, chiefly in infancy and early childhood and most evident where a second immune defect coexists. Its status as a consequence of isolated MBL deficiency is disputed, and the entry carries that dispute: a 5-year follow-up cohort found no difference in respiratory outcomes between MBL-deficient and MBL-sufficient children. No frequency band is tagged, because the proportion affected comes from referral cohorts and cannot be generalised to all deficient individuals.

nodes.description: The opposing branch of the "MBL paradox": because MBL-mediated opsonisation can facilitate complement-assisted entry of some intracellular organisms, reduced MBL is associated with lower susceptibility to tuberculosis and modifies leprosy. This node records that reduced lectin-pathway activation is not uniformly harmful; it is a protective association, not a route to the disease's infection phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: A Meta-analysis of MBL2 Polymorphisms and Tuberculosis Risk.
evidence.snippet: MBL2 rs1800450 and rs1800451 polymorphisms play a protective role in TB infection and reinforce their critical significance as a potential genetic marker for TB resistance.

evidence.reference_title: Mannose-binding lectin deficiency and respiratory tract infection.
evidence.snippet: Intracellular infections like tuberculosis may be less common with MBL deficiency because of reduced opsonophagocytosis.

nodes.description: With less C3b and less surface-bound MBL, neutrophils and macrophages take up and kill susceptible extracellular microbes less efficiently; MBL also acts as a direct opsonin independent of C3b. In human monocyte-derived macrophages, opsonising Neisseria meningitidis with MBL increased capture and doubled internalisation, so loss of MBL removes a measurable opsonic contribution. This is the effector step whose weakening underlies the infection susceptibility, but on its own it is usually compensated by antibody, the other complement pathways and neutrophils.
